---
title: "Alternative case definitions (exhaustive search)"
output: html_document
---

Reproduces **Table 5** (aged 14 and over), **Table S6** (aged 14 and over with confirmed hepatitis E defined by the presence of HEV RNA, South Sudan) and **Table S7** (children under 14, South
Sudan). Every combination of signs/symptoms is evaluated as "acute jaundice and at
least one" or "at least two" of the listed symptoms.

**Selection rule.** For each population and rule, find the highest joint threshold
(10%, 20%, ..., 90%) that at least one informative definition (sensitivity +
specificity > 1) exceeds on both sensitivity and specificity. Among the definitions
above that threshold, report the one with the highest specificity, breaking ties by
sensitivity and then by fewest symptoms. The threshold used is shown next to each
selected definition. Without a threshold, the highest-specificity informative
definition is a single rare symptom such as itch, with about 4% sensitivity.

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
library(here)
source(here("R", "data.R"))
source(here("R", "metrics.R"))
source(here("R", "combos.R"))

ssd_igm <- load_ssd(binary = TRUE)                       # reference test: IgM
ssd_pcr <- load_ssd(binary = TRUE, outcome = "pcr")      # reference test: PCR

populations <- list(
  `South Sudan` = list(dat = ssd_igm, symptoms = SSD_SYMPTOMS),
  `South Sudan PCR` = list(dat = ssd_pcr, symptoms = SSD_SYMPTOMS),
  `South Sudan children` = list(dat = load_ssd(children = TRUE, binary = TRUE), symptoms = SSD_SYMPTOMS),
  Bangladesh = list(dat = load_bd(binary = TRUE), symptoms = BD_SYMPTOMS)
)

# Populations and rules analysed here (the combined analysis is notebook 04)
analyses <- filter(CASE_DEF_ANALYSES, population != "Combined")
```

```{r search}
results <- analyses %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(all_defs = list(evaluate_case_defs(populations[[population]]$dat,
                                            populations[[population]]$symptoms, min_k)),
         n_defs = nrow(all_defs),
         n_informative = sum(all_defs$informative),
         threshold = highest_threshold(all_defs)) %>%
  ungroup()

results %>% select(population, min_k, n_defs, n_informative, threshold)
```

## Table 5 and Table S7 and Table S8

```{r selected}
selected <- results %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(best = list(format_selected(add_wilson_ci(select_case_defs(all_defs, threshold))))) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(population, min_k, threshold, best) %>%
  tidyr::unnest(best) %>%
  as.data.frame()
selected
```

## Sensitivity/specificity of all informative definitions

```{r plot, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 6}
results %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(all_defs = list(filter(all_defs, informative))) %>%
  tidyr::unnest(all_defs) %>%
  ggplot2::ggplot(ggplot2::aes(specificity, sensitivity)) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(alpha = 0.2, size = 0.6) +
  ggplot2::facet_grid(paste("at least", min_k) ~ population) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal()
```
